reading.body:
Idaho's tracked data center footprint consists of two facilities, neither of which has a reported power draw, leaving the state's contribution to AI compute infrastructure effectively unmeasured by this data.

The two facilities sit in Rexburg and Bear Lake County. One is operated by The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints as a Family History Center, a use case oriented toward archival storage rather than high-density compute. The other, VentureData in Rexburg, carries no operator or capacity information here. With total megawatts recorded as zero, the data cannot support any claim about power demand, grid load, or AI workload capacity for either site.

What this data does cover is geographic presence and facility identity, nothing more. It does not cover colocation capacity, power contracts, connectivity, or whether either facility hosts any AI workload at all. Idaho has significant hydroelectric resources that make it theoretically attractive for power-intensive compute, but that context is absent from this data and cannot be read into it.

facilities.name: Family History Center
facilities.operator: The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
